_about: Proposal definitions for the noisy-shop demo world. Status and timestamps come from fixtures/scenario.json. Explanations are templates: {placeholders} are filled by server/server/engine.py from computed numbers, [n] links to the numbered evidence the server builds (1 volume, 2 usage, 3 dry run, 4 guardrails).

notes.openpipeline: Stage and processor names follow the OpenPipeline processing docs. The exact configuration-API JSON keys are not verified yet. TODO(verify): https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/platform/openpipeline/concepts/processing
notes.otel: Format follows the opentelemetry-collector-contrib READMEs (filter processor format for v0.146.0+). Not checked with otelcol validate: fixture mode has no collector.

proposals.title: Drop DEBUG logs from payment
explanation: payment writes {records_day} DEBUG records a day, {gib_day}, which is {share} of its log volume [1].
Nothing has read them in the last 30 days: no query, dashboard, notebook, workflow or alert. The last query was {last_used} [2].
The Payments overview dashboard and the Payment failures alert read INFO and ERROR only, so they keep working [2].
The matcher selects DEBUG and nothing else. In the dry run it hit {errors_matched} ERROR or FATAL records [3].
Dropping them saves about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month at your rates.

otel.code:
processors:
  filter/sift-payment-debug:
    error_mode: ignore
    log_conditions:
      - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "payment" and log.severity_number >= SEVERITY_NUMBER_DEBUG and log.severity_number < SEVERITY_NUMBER_INFO

proposals.title: Drop GET /healthz spans from frontend
explanation: Kubernetes probes call GET /healthz on every frontend pod several times a second: {records_day} spans a day, {share} of frontend span volume [1].
No query, dashboard, workflow or alert has read these spans in 30 days [2].
The rule drops successful probes only (status 200), so a failing health check is still traced [3].
The Frontend latency dashboard reads GET /api/products and is not affected [2].
Dropping them saves about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month at your rates.

otel.code:
processors:
  filter/sift-frontend-healthz:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_conditions:
      - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "frontend" and span.attributes["http.route"] == "/healthz" and span.attributes["http.response.status_code"] == 200

proposals.title: Drop re-logged stack traces from cart, keep the first
explanation: When a call to inventory times out, cart logs the same 45-line stack trace three times: in InventoryClient, again in CartService and again in CartController [1].
The rule drops the two re-logged copies and keeps the original from InventoryClient, so every timeout is still logged once [3].
The only reads in 30 days were {queries_30d} triage queries during INC-2291. They search for the message text and still find the original [2].
That removes {matched} of {scope_records} cart log records a day and saves about {save_eur_month} a month.
Confidence is medium: the rule relies on code.function.name. If cart is refactored, the copies stop matching and nothing is dropped by mistake.

openpipeline.matcher: matchesValue(service.name, "cart") and matchesPhrase(content, "Timeout calling inventory") and code.function.name != "InventoryClient.reserve"

otel.code:
processors:
  filter/sift-cart-dup-trace:
    error_mode: ignore
    log_conditions:
      - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "cart" and IsMatch(log.body, "^Timeout calling inventory") and log.attributes["code.function.name"] != "InventoryClient.reserve"

proposals.title: Turn inventory heartbeat logs into a metric
explanation: Each inventory worker logs "heartbeat ok" every second: {records_day} lines a day, {share} of inventory log volume [1].
Nothing has queried these lines in 30 days [2].
The rule counts them into the metric inventory.heartbeat.count before the raw lines are dropped, so a silent worker is still visible [3].
That saves about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month after the cost of the new metric.

openpipeline.processor: Counter metric, then No storage assignment

otel.code:
connectors:
  count/sift-inventory-heartbeat:
    logs:
      inventory.heartbeat.count:
        description: Heartbeat lines from inventory workers
        conditions:
          - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "inventory" and IsMatch(body, "^heartbeat ok")

processors:
  filter/sift-inventory-heartbeat:
    error_mode: ignore
    log_conditions:
      - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "inventory" and IsMatch(log.body, "^heartbeat ok")

# Wire the count connector as an exporter of the logs pipeline (before the filter)
# and as a receiver of the metrics pipeline.

proposals.title: Remove user.id from http.server.request.duration
explanation: The user.id dimension puts a visitor UUID on every http.server.request.duration data point, which multiplies the number of series [1].
The Frontend latency and Executive Revenue dashboards and the High latency frontend alert read this metric. They split by service.name and http.route, never by user.id [2].
Removing the dimension keeps all of them working. Only per-user splits go away, and nobody uses them [3].
That saves about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month at your rates.

otel.code:
processors:
  transform/sift-drop-user-id:
    error_mode: ignore
    metric_statements:
      - context: datapoint
        conditions:
          - metric.name == "http.server.request.duration"
        statements:
          - delete_key(datapoint.attributes, "user.id")

proposals.title: Mask customer email addresses in email logs
explanation: The email service writes the customer's address in clear text on every order confirmation: {records_day} records a day [1].
Support's Email delivery audit notebook reads these lines, so dropping them is not an option [2].
The rule masks the address to ***@*** and leaves the rest of the line intact. Order IDs and timestamps stay searchable [3].
This saves no money. It removes personal data from {gib_month} of logs a month.

openpipeline.matcher: matchesValue(service.name, "email") and matchesPhrase(content, "Sent confirmation to user")

otel.code:
processors:
  transform/sift-redact-email:
    error_mode: ignore
    log_statements:
      - context: log
        conditions:
          - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "email"
        statements:
          - replace_pattern(log.body, "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "***@***")

proposals.title: Remove db.statement from inventory SELECT spans
explanation: Inventory's SELECT spans carry the full SQL text in db.statement: {gib_day} a day [1].
When this was proposed, no parsed query or dashboard referenced db.statement. One dashboard tile used a variable the parser could not resolve [2].
Dropping the attribute would save about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month.

otel.code:
processors:
  transform/sift-drop-db-statement:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
      - context: span
        conditions:
          - span.name == "SELECT inventory.stock"
        statements:
          - delete_key(span.attributes, "db.statement")

proposals.title: Drop static asset spans from frontend
explanation: Spans for static assets (GET /static/*) are {gib_day} a day, {share} of frontend span volume [1].
Nobody has queried them in 30 days [2].
Dropping them saves about {save_gib_month} and {save_eur_month} a month at your rates.

otel.code:
processors:
  filter/sift-frontend-static:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_conditions:
      - resource.attributes["service.name"] == "frontend" and IsMatch(span.attributes["url.path"], "^/static/")
